## What it catches

A Security record that a member was added to a global, local or universal security group whose name is one of the built-in privileged groups. Adding an account to such a group is the shortest way to give it lasting administrative rights. Rights granted through nested groups, delegation or other groups than those listed are not seen.

```yaml
selection:
  EventID:
  - 4728
  - 4732
  - 4756
  TargetUserName:
  - Domain Admins
  - Enterprise Admins
  - Schema Admins
  - Administrators
  - Backup Operators
  - Account Operators
  - DnsAdmins
condition: selection
```

## Tested on

- fires: `member added to Domain Admins`
- fires: `member added to Enterprise Admins`
- fires: `member added to Schema Admins`
- fires: `member added to the local Administrators of a server`
- fires: `member added to Backup Operators`
- fires: `member added to Account Operators`
- fires: `member added to DnsAdmins`
- quiet: `member added to a remote access group`
- quiet: `member added to Remote Desktop Users of a server`
- quiet: `member removed from Domain Admins`
- quiet: `member added to a universal distribution of printers' administrators`
- quiet: `the Domain Admins group itself changed`

## False positives

- Approved changes: a new administrator joining the team or a service account being set up
- Identity management tools that re-apply group membership

## What it does not see

- Rights gained through a nested group, a delegated permission or a group not in the list
- Groups renamed or translated by the operating system's language
- Domain controllers or servers whose Security log is not collected, or whose audit policy omits group management

## First checks

- Read who added the member and which account was added, in the full record on the host
- Match the change with a ticket or an owner
- Review what the added account did after the change
